# Surfaces (docs/surface-protocol.md): a program (surface-probe.py, through
# tools/surface/surface.py) asks, draws a card in its output, hears a choice,
# a typed note and a click, updates the card and draws an overlay. When it
# ends, the overlay goes and the card stays in the output, dimmed, its
# controls off; the screen cleared under it, it goes. Run with --persist
# too: the bytes go through liberttyd, and a second window on the session
# gets its screen back, without the surfaces (they're the window's).
# @TOOLS@: tools/surface; @DIR@: this test's folder.
type:python3 @DIR@/surface-probe.py @TOOLS@
key:enter
wait:2.0
expect:SUPPORTED 1
expect:SHOWN
expect-surface:demo
expect-surface-text:demo=Deploy now?
expect-surface-text:demo=From
expect-surface-live:demo=yes
surface-choose:demo=env=prod
wait:0.6
expect:EVENT select env  prod
surface-submit:demo=note=hello
wait:0.6
expect:EVENT submit note hello
surface-press:demo=deploy
wait:1.0
expect:EVENT click deploy hello
expect-surface-text:demo=Deploying
expect-surface:ov
wait:2.0
expect:DONE
wait:0.8
# The program ended: its overlay went, its card stays, dimmed.
expect-no-surface:ov
expect-surface:demo
expect-surface-live:demo=no
# The shell got nothing of the protocol's.
expect-not:7502
# The screen cleared: the card goes up into the scrollback with the output
# it was in, out of view.
type:clear
key:enter
wait:1.2
expect-no-surface:demo
# A program that shows a card and ends at once: the card stays above the
# prompt, ended (the prompt isn't taken for the card's own program's time).
type:printf '\n\n\n\033]7502;s;{"id":"quick","rows":3,"elements":[{"type":"text","text":"Q"}]}\a'
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-surface:quick
expect-surface-live:quick=no
# One drawn from the cursor's row down, where the prompt then draws: gone.
type:printf '\033]7502;s;{"id":"under","rows":2,"anchor":"cursor","elements":[{"type":"text","text":"U"}]}\a'
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-no-surface:under
# A flood: a hundred overlays (16 kept), cleared; then a thousand updates of
# one card: the rate holds them back, and the last is what shows.
type:clear; python3 @DIR@/surface-flood.py
key:enter
wait:0.8
expect-surface-count:16
wait:2.2
expect:FLOODED
expect-surface-text:card=update 999
